options.title: Match rooming pace to clinician capacity
options.description: Adjust the rooming pace to match the capacity of the clinicians, especially physicians, to ensure that patients do not experience long waits after rooming.
options.local_fit: This option fits well with the local context, as it addresses the observed slow physician pace and long waits after rooming. By adjusting the rooming pace, the hospital can potentially reduce the pressure on physicians and improve patient flow.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: If successful, this option may reduce the pressure on the Charge Nurse, as they will have to manage fewer escalations. However, it may also shift some pressure to the administration or scheduling team, who will need to ensure that the rooming and physician schedules are aligned.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the impact on wait times after rooming and the number of escalations. Compare these metrics to previous periods to assess the effectiveness of the adjustment.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the adjustment does not lead to a significant reduction in wait times or escalations, or if other factors (e.g., staffing issues) continue to impact physician pace.

options.title: Protect reserve monitored beds
options.description: Implement a process to protect a certain number of monitored beds for acute arrivals, especially for CTAS 1 or 2 patients, to ensure immediate access as required by policy.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with the policy expectation of immediate access to monitored beds for CTAS 1 or 2 patients. It can help address the issue of high bed occupancy and ensure that these patients receive the necessary level of care promptly.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Implementing this process may reduce the pressure on the Charge Nurse by providing a more structured approach to bed allocation. However, it may also shift pressure to the nursing staff responsible for managing the monitored beds, as they will need to ensure that the reserved beds are available when needed.
options.how_we_would_know: Track the number of CTAS 1 or 2 patients who are immediately assigned to monitored beds after arrival. Compare this to the number of patients who experience delays due to bed unavailability. Assess the impact on wait times and patient satisfaction.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the process does not lead to a significant improvement in immediate access to monitored beds for CTAS 1 or 2 patients, or if other factors (e.g., unexpected patient surges) continue to impact bed availability.

options.title: Learn more about physician pace
options.description: Conduct a deeper analysis of the factors influencing the physician pace. Understand the challenges they face and any potential barriers to timely patient assessment.
options.local_fit: No library evidence. This option provides an opportunity to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the situation. By learning more about the factors affecting physician pace, the hospital can develop more targeted solutions.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Learning more about physician pace may not directly reduce pressure on any specific role. However, it can provide valuable insights for future process adjustments or policy reviews.
options.how_we_would_know: Engage in discussions with physicians and nursing staff to understand their perspectives and challenges. Analyze patient flow data to identify patterns or trends that may be affecting physician pace.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the analysis does not reveal any significant insights or if the factors influencing physician pace are beyond the hospital's control.

recommendation.rationale: Matching rooming pace to clinician capacity directly addresses slow physician pace and long waits. Despite low evidence, this practical option fits the local context well.
recommendation.would_change_if: If analysis reveals external factors affecting physician pace, or if other evidence suggests a different approach.
